name: LMV393IDR
title: LMV331 single, LMV393 dual and LMV339 quad low-voltage comparators
summary: A family of general-purpose voltage comparators for 2.7 V to 5.5 V single supplies: the LMV331 has one comparator, the LMV393 two and the LMV339 four. They are the low-voltage counterparts of the LM393 and LM339 (which run from 5 V to 30 V) and draw far less supply current: 26 µA typical for the single LMV331. The input common-mode range reaches ground, and each output is an open NPN collector that sinks current and needs a pull-up. LMV393IDR is the dual in the 8-pin SOIC (D) on a 2500-piece reel.

circuits.title: Figure 7-1. Typical application: input against a reference
circuits.description: One comparator decides whether Vin is above or below a fixed Vref (2.5 V in the design example). Vin drives the non-inverting input and Vref the inverting input. The comparator runs from VSUP; its open-collector output is pulled up by RPULLUP to a separate logic rail VLOGIC, so the output level suits the logic it drives. CL is the load capacitance on the output. The output is high when Vin is above Vref and low when it is below.

operation.text: LMV393 (dual) and LMV339 (quad) are 2.7 V to 5.5 V versions of the LM393 and LM339, which run from 5 V to 30 V; LMV331 is the one-comparator member. They meet or better the LM393 and LM339 figures at a small part of their supply current.

Each input is a PNP stage. Its base-emitter drop caps the common-mode range: the inputs work from ground up to about 0.7 V below VCC. At VCC+ = 5 V the typical range at 25 °C is -0.1 V to 4.2 V, at 2.7 V it is -0.1 V to 2 V. Above or below 25 °C, VICR spans 0 V to VCC - 0.7 V, and inputs outside that span can give a wrong result.

The output is an NPN transistor with its emitter at GND and its collector open. It conducts and sinks current when the inverting input is above the non-inverting input by more than the offset voltage, and is off (high impedance, high through an external pull-up) otherwise. The low level behaves as a resistance: VOL rises with the sink current (Figure 5-3). The pull-up rail sets the output logic level independent of the supply, and the open output can be used for AND logic.

Both inputs in range: the output follows the sign of IN+ minus IN-, beyond the offset. IN- above the range with IN+ in it: output low, sinking. IN+ above the range with IN- in it: output high impedance. Both inputs above the range: output low, sinking.
Overdrive is how far the input difference goes past the offset voltage. It has to exceed VIO for a reliable decision, and more overdrive shortens the response (Figures 5-5 to 5-8 and 7-2).
The output edges are set by the load: the rising edge by RPULLUP charging CL, the falling edge by the output transistor's collector-emitter resistance discharging CL.
For a comparator design, settle in turn the input voltage range, the smallest overdrive, the output and drive current, and the response time.
Fast comparisons and noisy or AC inputs call for a bypass capacitor at the supply pin. Ripple on the supply moves the input common-mode range for a moment and can upset the result.

Without hysteresis the comparator needs a clean, steady supply. Place a bypass capacitor, 0.1 µF in the LMV331 example, from VCC to ground beside the supply pin; with a negative supply on GND, bypass that pin to ground with 0.1 µF as well. With a single supply, put no capacitor between the GND pin and system ground.
One output may be shorted to ground for an unlimited time at TA up to 25 °C with VCC up to 5.5 V. A short from an output to VCC heats the part and can destroy it.
